phases.name: Scope, Context & Credentials
phases.description: The operator adds what is already known before the engagement starts: scope, context and credentials. Only the operator can advance this phase.

steps.title: Set the Boundaries
steps.description: Record the in-scope IP ranges, CIDRs and hostnames, plus everything explicitly out of scope (third-party/shared hosting, production data, destructive tests, allowed scan intensity, rate limits, testing windows). Endpoints here are services, i.e. IP+port, not URLs. Later steps treat this as the hard limit.
steps.examples:
Scope: 203.0.113.0/24, mail.example.com, vpn.example.com
Out of scope: 203.0.113.10 (shared host), no DoS, scan <= 100 pkt/s

steps.title: Supply Context & Credentials
steps.description: Add what the client told you: what the perimeter is for, which systems are business-critical, known management interfaces, maintenance windows, and any test credentials for exposed services (VPN, portals, mail). Missing credentials limit authenticated checks later on.
steps.examples:
Context: internet perimeter of an SME; VPN gateway + mail + a marketing site.
Creds: one test VPN account, one webmail account.

phases.icon: <path d="M5 12.5a10 10 0 0 1 14 0M8 16a6 6 0 0 1 8 0" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" fill="none" stroke-linecap="round"/><circle cx="12" cy="19" r="1.5" fill="currentColor"/>
phases.name: Reachability
phases.description: Find out quickly what is alive and reachable in scope before spending time on full recon. Confirm discovered hosts are in scope before adding them.

steps.title: Ping Sweep
steps.description: Sweep the in-scope ranges to see which hosts answer. Many perimeter hosts block ICMP, so treat a silent host as 'unknown', not 'down' -- the next step and -Pn scans still cover it. Record the live hosts.
steps.examples:
nmap -sn 203.0.113.0/24 -oA sweep
fping -a -g 203.0.113.0/24 2>/dev/null

steps.title: Quick Port Scan (nmap -F)
steps.description: Run a fast top-ports scan across the live (and unknown) hosts to confirm what is exposed and spot anything unexpected before deeper recon. Add each live IP+port you confirm as an endpoint through /api/v1/endpoint/..
steps.examples:
nmap -Pn -F 203.0.113.0/24 -oA quick
nmap -Pn -F -sV <host>   # add versions on the open ports

phases.icon: <path d="M3 7l9-4 9 4-9 4-9-4z" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linejoin="round"/><path d="M3 12l9 4 9-4M3 17l9 4 9-4" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" fill="none" stroke-linejoin="round"/>
phases.name: Recon
phases.description: Enumerate the full attack surface. The goal here is coverage -- find every exposed service -- not exploitation. Add every discovered IP+port as an endpoint through /api/v1/endpoint/.. so later phases have full coverage.

steps.title: Top-1000 TCP Port Discovery (-Pn)
steps.description: Discover the common TCP services across all in-scope hosts with a top-1000 port scan. Use -Pn so hosts that block ping are still scanned. This is the primary discovery sweep; feed the open IP+ports into the endpoint list.
steps.examples:
nmap -Pn --top-ports 1000 -T4 203.0.113.0/24 -oA tcp-top1000
Then POST /api/v1/endpoint for each new IP:port.

steps.title: Full TCP Port Scan (-p-)
steps.description: Scan all 65535 TCP ports on the live hosts so nothing on a non-standard port is missed. Add any newly found IP+port as an endpoint.
steps.examples:
nmap -Pn -p- -T4 <host> -oA tcp-full
nmap -Pn -p- --min-rate 1000 <host>

steps.title: UDP Port Scan (-F) on Live Hosts
steps.description: Run a fast UDP scan on the discovered live hosts to catch UDP services (DNS, SNMP, NTP, IKE, etc.). UDP is slow and noisy -- keep it to the fast list and the hosts you confirmed live. Add new IP+ports as endpoints.
steps.examples:
nmap -Pn -sU -F <host> -oA udp-fast
nmap -Pn -sU -p 53,123,161,500 <host>

steps.title: Identify Basic Services / Grab Banners
steps.description: For every open port, detect the service and version and grab its banner. This turns 'open port' into 'what is actually running', which drives the per-service checks later. Record versions on each endpoint.
steps.examples:
nmap -Pn -sV -sC -p <ports> <host> -oA services
nc -nv <host> <port>   # raw banner
whatweb / curl -skI https://<host>:<port>

steps.title: Collect DNS & Certificate Names
steps.description: Resolve and reverse-resolve the hosts, and read the TLS certificate (subject + SAN) and certificate-transparency logs of every TLS port. These often reveal more hostnames, virtual hosts and staging systems. Only add names that are in scope; note the rest for the operator.
steps.examples:
dig +short -x <ip>
openssl s_client -connect <host>:443 </dev/null 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -ext subjectAltName
curl -s 'https://crt.sh/?q=%25.example.com&output=json' | jq -r '.[].name_value' | sort -u

steps.title: Screenshot Web Services
steps.description: Take a screenshot of every HTTP(S) service found, across all ports. A visual sweep is the fastest way to triage dozens of web endpoints: login portals, default pages, admin panels and forgotten apps stand out immediately. Attach the screenshots and note the interesting ones.
steps.examples:
gowitness scan file -f hosts-ports.txt
eyewitness --web -f urls.txt
httpx -l hosts.txt -ports 80,443,8080,8443 -screenshot

phases.icon: <circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M15 9l-2 4-4 2 2-4 4-2z" fill="currentColor"/>
phases.name: Free Agentic Recon
phases.description: Step back and look for recon gaps the structured steps missed. Recon only -- no exploitation here.

steps.title: Free-Form Recon
steps.description: Read GET /api/v1/notes and decide if anything is still missing recon-wise: a service whose version was not pinned, a host whose role is unclear, a UDP service not probed, a certificate name never followed up. Only act on real gaps and within the rules of engagement; otherwise finish with status=skipped.
steps.examples:
Targeted: a -sV --version-intensity 7 follow-up on one ambiguous banner.
Skipped: status=skipped, observations='Recon covered all in-scope hosts and ports; versions pinned.'

steps.title: Add Newly Found Endpoints
steps.description: Information-gathering only -- no new traffic to the target. Compare the stored endpoints against the scan outputs and notes. Add any IP+port not yet stored through /api/v1/endpoint/..; if nothing is new, finish with status=skipped.
steps.examples:
Added: observations='Full TCP scan found 8443/tcp on .20 not in the endpoint list -- added it.'
Skipped: status=skipped, observations='No new endpoints.'

phases.icon: <path d="M5 4h8a4 4 0 0 1 4 4v12H9a4 4 0 0 0-4-4V4z" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linejoin="round"/><path d="M9 8h4M9 12h5" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round"/>
phases.name: Infrastructure Understanding
phases.description: Build a model of the perimeter: host roles, which services are business-critical, management surfaces, authentication gateways and shared hosting. Then connect it back to the scope.

steps.title: Map Host Roles & Services
steps.description: For each host, decide what it is (mail, VPN, web app, DB, management, load balancer) from its open ports, banners and certificate names. A clear role map tells you where the real risk sits.
steps.examples: Playwright/curl the web services; note mail on 25/465/587, VPN on 500/4500, etc.

steps.title: Identify Trust Boundaries
steps.description: Security is about breaking boundaries. On an external perimeter the main ones are: internet vs internal, authenticated vs anonymous, and one tenant/customer vs another on shared services. Which boundary would hurt most if it broke here?

steps.title: Identify Critical Systems & Shared Services
steps.description: Pick out the systems whose compromise matters most (VPN/remote access, mail, anything exposing a database or management plane) and the shared services that many hosts depend on. These get the deepest testing.

steps.title: Research Known Vulnerabilities
steps.description: For every identified product, service and version, search for known CVEs, public exploits and default credentials. Only note issues that plausibly apply to the observed versions; they become concrete per-endpoint tests later.
steps.examples:
searchsploit <product> <version>
Search NVD / vendor advisories for '<service> <version>'

steps.title: Connect to the Initial Scope
steps.description: Put the initial project information and scope into perspective with what recon actually found. Does the exposed surface match what the client expected, or is something unexpected reachable?

phases.icon: <rect x="5" y="4" width="14" height="16" rx="2" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M9 9h6M9 13h3M15 13v6M12 16h6" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round"/>
phases.name: Modify Checklist
phases.description: Tune the project checklist to this perimeter before working it: drop checks for protocols that are not present, add target-specific ones, and deepen the checks that matter.

steps.title: Tune the Checklist
steps.description: Review the checklist against this target. Mark irrelevant checks 'not applicable' with a one-line reason (e.g. no SMB exposed), and add any check that is missing for a discovered service. Be careful removing checks -- better a bit too much than a gap. Use the API -- notes alone do not change the checklist. Summarise in this step's observations how many you marked not applicable and the rough categories.

steps.title: Increase Check Runs
steps.description: For which checks would a deeper look pay off on this perimeter (TLS across many hosts, the VPN/mail gateways, any exposed admin plane)? Increase the runs for those so they get a thorough pass.

phases._comment: Phase id MUST stay 'general_checks': the workflow page hardcodes that id to render the checklist panel (workflow.html + routes.py).
phases.icon: <path d="M12 2l8 3v6c0 5-3.5 9-8 11-4.5-2-8-6-8-11V5l8-3z" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linejoin="round"/><path d="M9 12l2 2 4-4" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" fill="none" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/>
phases.name: Work on Checklist
phases.description: Work every global-scope check. These are the fast, perimeter-wide checks -- a lot of them are TLS -- so move quickly. The endpoint/service checks are worked later. The phase advances only after every global-check is finished.

steps.title: Work the Global Checks
steps.description: Work every global-scope check. Focus it, do real testing instead of trusting old notes, record what you did and found, then finish it. These are perimeter-wide, so keep them quick. For the TLS checks especially: test all TLS ports at once (e.g. with testssl/sslscan), and when a weakness holds, write ONE finding that lists every affected IP+port in its description rather than one finding per host. Any weakness you confirm, immediately write or update an issue via /api/v1/finding.
steps.examples:
POST /api/v1/check/{id}/focus
testssl.sh --file hosts-ports.txt   # one sweep across all TLS services
...then: POST /api/v1/finding {"title":"Deprecated TLS protocols enabled","severity":"medium","description":"Affected: 203.0.113.5:443, 203.0.113.5:8443, 203.0.113.9:443 ..."}
POST /api/v1/check/{id}/finish

phases.icon: <path d="M12 3l8 4.5v9L12 21l-8-4.5v-9L12 3z" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linejoin="round"/><path d="M4 7.5l8 4.5 8-4.5M12 12v9" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" fill="none" stroke-linejoin="round"/>
phases.name: Service and Host-Specific Checks
phases.description: Pull together every service endpoint (IP+port) discovered so far, organise them, then test each one for full coverage. Every open port gets checked.

steps.title: Collect Endpoints
steps.description: Information-gathering only. Review the scan outputs, notes and captures for services found so far and add each IP+port through /api/v1/endpoint/.. Do not run new scans here -- just make coverage complete.
steps.examples:
GET /api/v1/notes
Then POST /api/v1/endpoint for each IP:port not yet stored.

steps.title: Group by Feature
steps.description: Sort the endpoints into groups so related services are tested together -- by service type (all SMTP, all RDP, all web) or by host. Put endpoints that belong together into the same group.
steps.examples:
POST /api/v1/feature-groups  {"name": "Web services"}
PUT /api/v1/endpoint/{id}/feature-group  {"feature_group": "<group_id>"}

steps.title: Increase Endpoint Runs
steps.description: Which endpoints deserve a deeper look (a VPN or mail gateway, an exposed admin panel, a database port)? Increase the runs for those so they get a very thorough pass.

steps.title: Test All Endpoints
steps.description: Test every endpoint thoroughly, one group at a time. For each IP+port run the per-endpoint checks (default creds, anonymous access, weak/cleartext protocol, known CVEs, risky exposure, info disclosure), record observations and raw captures, set a status, then mark it tested. Any weakness you find, immediately write or update an issue via /api/v1/finding.
steps.examples:
POST /endpoint/{id}/focus -> POST /endpoint/{id}/checks-adjusted
GET /workflow/endpoint-testing/current-step?endpoint_id={id}
...test... PUT /check/{cid}/observations -> PUT /check/{cid}/status
Loop until done, then POST /endpoint/{id}/unfocus.

steps.title: Re-open Endpoints Worth Another Pass
steps.description: Testing one service often enables more on another: credentials from one host, a leaked internal name, an auth bypass. Read the notes and findings, re-open the endpoints that deserve another pass with the new knowledge and test them again. If nothing warrants it, finish with status=skipped.
steps.examples:
GET /api/v1/notes
Re-open an RDP host after finding reused credentials on an exposed service.

steps.title: Final Coverage Verification
steps.description: Please run a final verification: review the recon results, confirm that every discovered port has been recorded in the endpoints, and make sure each of those ports has been thoroughly tested. Try to do this verification in a different context window so you are not biased by the testing you just did. Re-open and finish any endpoint that was missed or only shallowly tested.
steps.examples:
GET /api/v1/notes  (re-read the recon/scan outputs)
GET /api/v1/endpoints  (confirm every discovered IP+port is stored)
For each port, confirm its per-endpoint checks are finished; re-open and test any gap.

phases.icon: <rect x="3" y="5" width="18" height="14" rx="2" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M3 9h18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="6" cy="7" r="0.7" fill="currentColor"/><circle cx="8.5" cy="7" r="0.7" fill="currentColor"/>
phases.name: Web Applications
phases.description: Any HTTP(S) service found on the in-scope hosts is a web application worth its own look. Do focused web recon on each, hunt for the high and medium risk web issues, and write up what you confirm.

steps.title: Web App Recon
steps.description: For every HTTP(S) service on the in-scope hosts, do focused web recon. Pull robots.txt and sitemap.xml, read the HTML source and linked JavaScript for comments, API paths, keys, internal hostnames and other sensitive information, and brute-force directories and files with a wordlist of roughly 20k entries using ffuf (or a similar tool) to discover hidden endpoints. Record every new path/endpoint you find and note anything sensitive. Keep request rates reasonable and in scope -- discovery only, do not hammer the server.
steps.examples:
ffuf -w wordlist-20k.txt -u https://<host>/FUZZ -mc 200,204,301,302,401,403 -t 40
curl -s https://<host>/robots.txt ; curl -s https://<host>/sitemap.xml
curl -s https://<host>/ | grep -iE 'api|token|secret|key|internal|todo'   # review HTML/JS source

steps.title: Find High & Medium Web Issues
steps.description: Test the discovered web apps for the issues that actually matter: authentication and session weaknesses, broken access control / IDOR, injection (SQLi, command, template), SSRF, insecure file upload or inclusion, exposed admin/debug interfaces, and components with known CVEs. Focus on reliable high and medium severity issues rather than low-severity noise. Test carefully and non-destructively, stay in scope, and on production keep to low-risk, read-only verification; never run denial-of-service or stress testing. As soon as you confirm an issue, write or update a finding via /api/v1/finding.
steps.examples:
Probe auth/session, access control (IDOR), injection and SSRF on the discovered endpoints.
POST /api/v1/finding  {"title": "Broken access control (IDOR)", "severity": "high", "description": "..."}

steps.title: Write Up Web Findings
steps.description: Turn every confirmed web issue into a clear, evidenced finding: start with what the problem is in simple words, then why it matters, then the technical detail and reproduction, and finish with a recommended fix plus a quick-fix alternative. Attach the supporting requests/responses, and a screenshot for any finding rated medium or higher. Keep one finding per distinct issue; if the same issue affects several apps, list every affected URL in that one finding.
steps.examples:
POST /api/v1/finding  {"title": "SQL injection in search", "severity": "high", "description": "..."}
PUT /api/v1/finding/{id}/raw-captures   (attach request/response and a screenshot)

phases.icon: <path d="M12 3l2 5 5 2-5 2-2 5-2-5-5-2 5-2 2-5z" fill="currentColor"/><circle cx="19" cy="5" r="1.5" fill="currentColor"/><circle cx="5" cy="19" r="1.5" fill="currentColor"/>
phases.name: Free Testing
phases.description: Anything the structured phases missed? Chase hunches and follow up on what you have found.

steps.title: Refine Notes
steps.description: The notes should not be a simple log of what happened. They should reflect a holistic view of the perimeter: what is exposed, what matters most, and what an external attacker would go for first. What were the operators of this perimeter trying to achieve, and did they miss something? Rewrite the notes to contain both a structured overview of this test plus the holistic risk view.

steps.title: Free-Form Testing
steps.description: Follow up on anything the structured phases did not cover: an odd service, a suspicious response, a trust relationship between two hosts. Record what you try and what comes of it. Start this free-form pass in a new context window so you come at the target fresh and are not biased by the structured testing you just did.
steps.examples:
Probe an unusual high port with multiple protocol clients.
Replay a login against the VPN/webmail with a tampered parameter.

phases.name: Attack Chaining
phases.description: From the findings so far: can we do more with them? Do they open new recon, apply to other hosts/services, or chain into something bigger?

steps.title: Push Each Finding Further
steps.description: Take each finding a bit further to understand its real impact, but stay careful: the aim is a slightly deeper look, not a full exploit. For example, confirm that default credentials actually log in and note what the account can see without changing anything, or check whether an exposed database port accepts an anonymous read-only connection. Prove the point with the lightest, lowest-risk check and prefer read-only, non-destructive evidence. Never modify, delete or corrupt data, and never run anything that could disrupt a service: no denial-of-service or stress testing. On production systems keep strictly to low-risk, read-only verification; if going further would risk availability or integrity, stop and describe the potential impact instead of demonstrating it. Update the finding's severity and evidence with what you safely confirm.
steps.examples:
Default creds on a device -> what does the account actually grant?
Exposed DB port -> does it allow an anonymous connection?

steps.title: Recon From Findings
steps.description: Use what the findings exposed (leaked hostnames, internal IPs, credentials, stack traces) as new recon input. Add new endpoints through /api/v1/endpoint/.. and note new hosts for the operator if they are out of scope.
steps.examples:
A certificate SAN reveals an internal VPN name -> follow it up if in scope.
Reused creds -> try them against other exposed services.

steps.title: Map to Other Checks
steps.description: Check whether each finding's root cause also applies elsewhere: the same weak TLS config on sibling hosts, the same default credentials on other devices, the same cleartext protocol on another port. Re-open and update the affected checks and endpoints.
steps.examples: Weak TLS on one host -> confirm the rest and add them to the same TLS finding's affected list.

steps.title: Test Attack Chains
steps.description: Combine weak signals and low findings into a chain with real impact and test it end to end. Write a finding for the chain itself, referencing the individual findings, with the full reproduction.
steps.examples:
Exposed management plane + default credentials -> device takeover.
Information disclosure + reused password -> authenticated access to a second service.

phases.icon: <circle cx="11" cy="11" r="6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M20 20l-4-4" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round"/><path d="M11 8.5v5M8.5 11h5" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round"/>
phases.name: Additional Work
phases.description: Before writing anything up, do the extra work that pays off: dig deeper where a vulnerability is likely hiding, then prune anything that will not hold up. Only confirmed, reproducible issues should reach Finding Writing.

steps.title: Deep-Dive Where It Pays Off
steps.description: Read GET /api/v1/notes and review the testing so far, then pick the spots where a deeper hunt is worth it -- a high-value gateway, a half-explored service, an ambiguous version. Dig into those hard and test them properly. If nothing warrants it, finish with status=skipped. Update the checklist checks and endpoint observations if you found new facts.
steps.examples:
Re-examine a service that returned odd errors with targeted, documented probes.
Skipped: status=skipped, observations='Coverage was thorough; no area warrants a deeper dive.'

steps.title: Identify False Positives
steps.description: Go back over every suspected weakness and reproduce it from scratch. Discard anything that does not hold up, and keep a clean reproduction plus evidence for the ones that do. Record the verdict for each so Finding Writing only sees confirmed, reproducible issues.
steps.examples:
Re-run the exact probe that triggered the issue and confirm it is consistent.
Discard a 'weak cipher' flagged by one tool but not reproducible with a handshake.

phases.icon: <path d="M5 3v18" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round"/><path d="M5 4h13l-3 4 3 4H5" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linejoin="round"/>
phases.name: Finding Writing
phases.description: Turn every confirmed weakness into a clear, evidenced finding.

steps.title: Write Up Findings
steps.description: Create a finding for every confirmed weakness with a clear title, a severity and a description of impact and reproduction. For perimeter-wide issues (especially TLS), write ONE finding and list every affected IP+port in the description rather than one per host. Attach the supporting raw captures so each finding stands on its own. The description should start with 1) what the problem is in simple non-technical words, then 2) a 'so-what' section on why it matters, then 3) the technical detail. The recommendation should give the proper fix plus a quick-fix alternative. Do not give the paragraphs extra headers. Try to overall user rather simple words so it is good to understand. Do not use long dashes
steps.examples:
POST /api/v1/finding  {"title": "Weak TLS configuration", "severity": "medium", "description": "Affected: 203.0.113.5:443, 203.0.113.9:443, ..."}
PUT /api/v1/finding/{id}/raw-captures  (attach the testssl output)

steps.title: Screenshot Medium+ Findings
steps.description: Every finding rated medium, high or critical must carry at least one screenshot as evidence. Review each finding's severity and attach a screenshot to any that is medium or higher. Info/low findings do not require one. Install the tools you need to capture evidence. Make sure you really take the screenshots.
steps.examples:
GET /api/v1/findings  (review each finding's severity)
POST /api/v1/finding/{id}/raw-captures  (attach a screenshot for each medium-or-higher finding)
